approachQuestion.prompt:
Keep the Marked Rooms. Each node of a binary tree stores a unique ID and a Boolean marked flag. Return a new tree containing exactly the nodes that lie on some path from the original root to a marked node. Preserve original left/right positions and IDs of retained nodes. If no node is marked, return null. Do not mutate the input.

Example 1: Input: root A unmarked; A.left=B unmarked; B.left=D marked; A.right=C unmarked; all other children missing. Output: A with left child B with left child D; all other pointers missing. Example 2: Input: one unmarked node A. Output: null. Example 3: Input: one marked node A. Output: a new marked node A.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; IDs are unique signed 32-bit integers. The input has child pointers only, no cycles or shared nodes, and arbitrary shape. Returned nodes are newly allocated and retain the original marked flags. Allocate a new node only after deciding it will be part of the final output.

options.text: Use postorder frames returning the retained child roots. If the current node is marked or either retained child exists, create its output copy with those children; otherwise return null.
options.feedback: A subtree contributes exactly when it contains a mark. A retained child therefore keeps all ancestors needed to connect it to the original root.

options.text: For each original node separately search its entire subtree for any mark. Build an output copy precisely when that search succeeds, preserving each retained child position.
options.feedback: This applies the correct retention test at every node, but repeated mark searches overlap. Child results already tell whether a mark exists below.

options.text: Delete every unmarked node and return only marked nodes in their original child slots, discarding children when their parent is deleted.
options.feedback: Example 1 would delete A and B, losing marked D even though both ancestors are required in the output.

options.text: Retain a node only if it is marked or has an immediately marked child.
options.feedback: In Example 1 A has no immediately marked child, but must remain because D is a marked descendant.

feedback.reason: A node is retained when its subtree contains a mark; unmarked ancestors may still be necessary connectors.
details: Use fixed-size postorder frames. A missing child returns null. After both children return their retained roots, create a copy of the current node only when its flag is marked or a returned child is non-null. Connect those returned children in the same slots. Otherwise return null. Pass the new root upward and release completed frames.

Keep an unmarked node when either retained child exists: it connects marked descendants to the root. Allocate a copy only after child decisions are known. Returned retained subtrees are output, while active postorder frames remain auxiliary.

“Use postorder frames returning the retained child roots. If the current node is marked or either retained child exists, create its output copy with those children; otherwise return null.”: A subtree contributes exactly when it contains a mark. A retained child therefore keeps all ancestors needed to connect it to the original root.

“Retain a node only if it is marked or has an immediately marked child.”: In Example 1 A has no immediately marked child, but must remain because D is a marked descendant.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed retention method consider n>=1 input nodes and input height h in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case pair. Count active frames and their two returned child pointers. Exclude the immutable input and every newly allocated node in the final output, including a completed output subtree awaiting attachment to its parent. Node allocation is constant-time and no output nodes are later discarded.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Inspect every input node once; active frames, rather than returned copies, determine helper space.
details: Each input node is inspected and combined once, with at most one constant-time output allocation. Only an active ancestor chain of O(h) fixed-size frames is auxiliary; completed retained subtrees belong to the output.

Inductively the returned child root is null exactly when that child subtree has no marked node. A current mark or non-null retained child is therefore equivalent to membership on a root-to-mark path. Creating no other nodes gives exactly the required output.

“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each input node is inspected and combined once, with at most one constant-time output allocation. Only an active ancestor chain of O(h) fixed-size frames is auxiliary; completed retained subtrees belong to the output.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
